transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-11
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Clara Nguyen (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood Prod Ops), Alicia Mora (CISO, Silverpine), Derek Holt (Head of Platform), Priya Sengupta (SRE), Evan Park (Legal)

Summary (auto): quick readout focused on security and continuity. Some technical deep dive on KMS and private deployment. Agreed actions and pilot.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. we're going to run through SOC2/ISO posture first then SSO/RBAC, logs, and then the BCDR escalation flow which was the ask from Alicia last week.
[00:18] Alicia: thanks samir, yes important for us to understand single pane of responsibility. we run daily risk reviews and need to map your escalation to our incident response.
[00:31] Clara: great, i'll try to keep the technical bits clear — quick note some of the acronyms might come out wrong on the transcript, sam el stuff might be transcribed oddly.
[00:45] Derek: ha yeah that's fine. we care less about transcript than the content. our main constraints: data residency in eu-west-1, audit log retention for seven years, and rto of 30 minutes for auth flows and 4 hours for batch reindex.
[01:05] Samir: ok noted. on SOC 2 we are Type II, our control matrix maps to common criteria, and we have an ISO 27001 certificate pending re-audit in q2. i'll drop the cert earlier.
[01:22] Alicia: are there any scoped exceptions? e.g., third-party subprocessors or dev environments that are out of scope?
[01:32] Marcus: yes good question. generally hosted offering uses managed cloud infra and a small set of CSP partners -- we disclose subprocessors in the security pack. dev lower environments can be excluded from SOC2 scope; production data is segregated.
[01:46] Priya: how are audit logs handled? we're after tamper-evident logs with export for SIEM ingestion, and immutable retention policy.
[02:00] Clara: logs are shipped to a customer-dedicated bucket in your region if in private deployment; for hosted we retain per-tenant logs for 90 days by default and can configure longer retention on request. audit trails are signed with envelope markers, but i do want to flag that our hosted logging currently uses customer-key-wrapped storage; we support KMS integration —
[02:22] Alicia: by KMS integration you mean we can bring our own key (BYOK)?
[02:26] Clara: yes BYOK supported for Private and Dedicated offerings; for hosted we support customer-managed keys in the cloud KMS in most regions and HSM-backed key wrap for more sensitive customers, there's an HSM option in our enterprise plan.
[02:39] Evan: does that include envelope encryption for token-cache and kv cache?
[02:44] Clara: yes, we do envelope encryption for token and kv cache. quick caveat, kv cache was sometimes transcribed as kv cash in previous meetings, so please ignore that. the cache keys are wrapped with your KMS key.
[02:57] Derek: what's the rotation policy? do you rotate keys automatically or do we manage rotations?
[03:03] Marcus: we support automated rotation with customer approval windows. rotations are logged and we retain pre-rotation keys per policy for decrypt within rpo windows if necessary.
[03:18] Priya: ok good. on SSO — we use Okta and need SAML + SCIM for provisioning plus RBAC roles that map to our internal groups. can we do attribute-based access?
[03:32] Clara: yes SAML + SCIM supported. RBAC model supports groups and attribute mapping. there are three built-in roles and you can add custom roles scoped to models or routes. small note, the SCIM endpoint needs to be allowed via a secure peering if using private deployment.
[03:48] Alicia: our legal team will need the SSO flow documented for contract. Evan: yes please include token expiry and service account behaviors.
[03:58] Evan: also curious about offline auditability for compliance. can we get time-window exports for auditors?
[04:04] Samir: yes we can provide time-bounded log exports and export hashes for chain of custody. we'll include that in the security pack.
[04:15] Derek: moving into BCDR — the ask was to see how Redwood handles failover. can you sketch the escalation matrix and typical RTO/RPO per tier?
[04:26] Clara: sure. we have three failover tiers: 1) node-level graceful fallback within same cluster (sub-second token continuity for in-flight requests, typical rto < 30s), 2) zone/region failover via replicated state and prefix caching (rto minutes, depends on seq length and kv warmup), 3) full account-level cross-region failover to a cold replica (rto hours, rpo depends on replication window).
[04:50] Priya: what's the replication cadence for the cold replica? near real-time or batched?
[04:55] Marcus: it's near real-time for metadata and service state; for large prefix caches we do snapshot-ish replication and replay — that contributes to longer rto for large models. our recommended rpo for account-level is 15 minutes if you enable continuous journal replication.
[05:13] Alicia: is the rpo 15 minutes SLA guaranteed or is it best-effort?
[05:18] Samir: guaranteed for Dedicated and Private with SLA addendum; hosted has configurable tiers and we can negotiate a stricter SLA in enterprise contracts.
[05:28] Derek: what happens operationally during an escalation? who notifies whom and how do we integrate with our pager?
[05:34] Clara: we have an escalation playbook: on detection we create an incident in our tracking system, page the on-call (SE/Infra), then tiered notifications to AE + CSM. for customers on a private deployment we can integrate with customer Ops' PagerDuty webhook to forward alerts.
[05:49] Priya: do you provide runbook steps we can consume into our automation?
[05:53] Marcus: yes we'll share a runbook template. in the pilot we usually collaborate to customize the runbook and smoke tests.
[06:00] Evan: legal question — how do you handle notification windows for breaches? contract min 72-hour notification is typical for us.
[06:07] Samir: we adhere to contractual notification windows; our standard is 72 hours for confirmed data breaches, with an initial alert within 24 hours for suspected incidents. clause can be tightened if needed.
[06:18] Alicia: can you confirm audit log retention for hosted vs private? you said 90 days default for hosted but we need 7 years preserved for financial audit in our eu region.
[06:28] Clara: for private deployment we can configure S3 or on-prem archival to meet 7-year retention. for hosted we can create a custom retention policy with egress to your long-term vault; that becomes an add-on. we'll include pricing.
[06:41] Derek: i'm worried about multi-tenant leakage in hosted — any hard tenancy separation guarantees?
[06:46] Marcus: multi-tenant is logically isolated at the request/tenant layer; for absolute separation we recommend Dedicated or Private where you get isolated GPU pools and VPC peering.
[06:58] Priya: next, testing — for the pilot we want to do a chaos scenario: simulate region failover and validate rto/rpo. are you okay running that?
[07:07] Clara: yes we typically do controlled failovers in the pilot. we'll need your authorization window and safe list of IPs. for hosted we schedule during low traffic and for private/deploy we coordinate runbook steps.
[07:19] Alicia: what about data residency controls during failover? we cannot failover data outside of EU jurisdiction for certain datasets.
[07:26] Samir: we can restrict failover targets by policy — you can pin failover to eu regions only, but that limits cross-region restarts. it's a policy decision tradeoff.
[07:37] Derek: okay makes sense. Marcus: technically on pinning we can region-route but there's a capacity tradeoff, we'll surface impact in the pilot.
[07:47] Evan: any FIPS compliance, HSM vendor details? we need vendor and certs for legal to verify.
[07:54] Clara: HSM options use AWS CloudHSM or Azure Dedicated HSM depending on region. we can provide vendor certs and HSM attestation reports as part of the security pack.
[08:07] Priya: if we request HSM-backed key wrap for logs, is performance impacted?
[08:13] Marcus: marginally for key operations, we do local caching of unwrapped keys for throughput; the token path uses wrapped keys but decrypts in an optimized path. you'll see small added latency on cold starts.
[08:25] Derek: let's talk SLA: what uptime do you commit to and what are credits/penalties?
[08:31] Samir: standard enterprise SLA is 99.9% monthly for critical inference endpoints for Dedicated; 99.95% possible with higher tier and multi-region redundancy; credits scale with downtime windows. we'll send the SLA doc.
[08:46] Alicia: link SLA to RTO for critical flows? we need explicit mapping in contract so we can map vendor SLA to our risk table.
[08:54] Samir: agree — we can add a mapping appendix.
[08:58] Derek: we've had a couple calls where edge cases around KV cache warmup caused longer latencies post-failover. can you provide mitigations?
[09:06] Marcus: yes, mitigation patterns: progressive failover, pre-warming caches via replay, and read-through fallback to a degraded model. we can also support persistent KV replication for critical prefixes at additional cost.
[09:20] Priya: how do you ensure graceful degradation? do you have multi-model fallback policies?
[09:25] Clara: yes fallback policies are first to a lower-cost compatible model, then to a canned response if necessary. fallbacks are configurable per route.
[09:34] Alicia: for compliance audits we need a clear change log for model rollouts and code that touches inference pipelines. do you provide those artifacts?
[09:42] Marcus: yes deployment and rollout logs, canary rollouts records, and change annotations are available via the console API and can be exported for audits.
[09:53] Evan: any legal restrictions on data sharing for debugging? we often need support to repro issues but must keep PII in our control.
[09:59] Samir: we have a support bundle workflow — you can enable scrubbing, or provide a hashed request snippet, or run local repro on a private deployment. support engineers sign this out and access is logged.
[10:14] Derek: ok let's talk timelines: we are aiming for a pilot in March and production by June if security is green. can Redwood commit to a security questionnaire fill within 48 hours?
[10:24] Clara: we'll have a partial questionnaire back in 48 hours and full pack by end of week, Feb 14.
[10:30] Priya: for the chaos test on the pilot — we need to define exact success criteria. RTO <= 30 mins for auth, RPO <= 15 minutes for core state, degraded latency < 2x baseline.
[10:42] Samir: noted, we will formalize acceptance criteria in the pilot plan.
[10:47] Alicia: on escalation contacts, here's our org: CISO -> Head of Platform -> Oncall SRE. we need Redwood to mirror that.
[10:56] Samir: yes we'll map to your escalation tiers and provide contact routing templates.
[11:02] Derek: any notable risks or single point of failure we should be aware of?
[11:07] Marcus: main risks: cross-region replication lag for large KV state, and capacity saturation if failover target isn't sized. we'll size dedicated capacity in the pilot and provide burst capacity options.
[11:19] Priya: do you offer a runbook-runthrough workshop? we prefer a tabletop before chaos tests.
[11:24] Clara: yes we do a tabletop with Ops and Security beforehand. that will be part of the pilot schedule.
[11:32] Evan: will you share sample contract language for SLA and notification windows? legal wants to start redlines early.
[11:38] Samir: i'll share the redlineable SLA and a notification template.
[11:43] Alicia: any thoughts on proving immutability of logs for auditors? we need tamper-evidence and chain-of-custody.
[11:50] Clara: we use append-only storage with signed manifests and provide hash chains for exported windows. auditors can verify via signature.
[11:58] Derek: excellent. last technical question — can models be pinned per-tenant to avoid accidental upgrades during a failover?
[12:04] Marcus: yes model pinning is supported; rollouts are explicit and require approvals configured in the console.
[12:11] Samir: ok i'm going to recap next steps then open to questions. recap: 1) samir to send SOC2/ISO overview + SLA + pricing, 2) clara to fill security questionnaire partial, 3) schedule pilot dry-run (tabletop) + chaos test week of feb 24, 4) silverpine to share BCDR runbook extract and target rto/rpo thresholds.
[12:35] Alicia: sounds good. one more: can we get a short note on data residency enforcement for EU datasets?
[12:41] Clara: yes we'll include a policy note showing routing controls and failover pinning.
[12:47] Evan: wrap up for legal: please include HSM vendor attestations and a redline sample for the 72-hour notification clause.
[12:56] Samir: noted. any other hand raises?
[13:00] (brief silence)
[13:07] Priya: none from me. thanks.
[13:10] Samir: great thanks everyone we'll follow up with the pack and scheduling invite for the tabletop.
[13:17] Derek: appreciate it.
[13:20] Alicia: thanks all.

(End of transcript)

Notes: Transcript contains minor mis-attributions and typical speech hesitations. Links referenced: Security packet (link: https://redwood.example.com/security-packet/silverpine), Pilot plan template (link: https://redwood.example.com/pilot-templates).
